messages:
incident-bot: Paging: SEV2 - Customer 'Sunnova' (private VPC, dedicated pool) reporting 50%+ request errors through their NLB -> ALB chain. Auto-alerts from healthchecks and SLOs triggered. Pinged on-call.

sasha (oncall): I’m on it. Can someone paste the latest target health from the customer NLB and the ALB target groups? Suspecting TG churn after last config push.

jamie (networking): grabbing it now. output from aws:

```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:targetgroup/tg-sunnova
{
  "TargetHealthDescriptions": [
    {"Target": {"Id": "10.0.12.45", "Port": 8443}, "TargetHealth": {"State": "unhealthy", "Reason": "TLS handshake error"}},
    {"Target": {"Id": "10.0.12.46", "Port": 8443}, "TargetHealth": {"State": "healthy"}},
    {"Target": {"Id": "10.0.12.47", "Port": 8443}, "TargetHealth": {"State": "unhealthy", "Reason": "Connection timed out"}}
  ]
}
```

jamie (networking): NLB health shows backend nodes flapping. Route53 healthchecks for the ALB are reporting failed probes from 3 locations. No recent infra autoscale events.

priya (acct-mgr): Sunnova complaining about 503s and partial search failures in prod. They say this started ~20m ago after a scheduled network rules update on their side. They’re on a Dedicated pool with VPC Private deployment. I’ve told them we’re investigating; they asked for a temporary failover if possible.

sasha (oncall): Noted. Possible paths: 1) quick rollback of their recent SG change (if customer agrees) 2) adjust NLB healthcheck protocol/port to match ALB termination 3) do DNS weighted failover to their backup ALB in us-west-2 (if they have one) 4) route through our regional proxy as short-term workaround. Which is feasible quickly?

jamie (networking): We can update the NLB healthcheck in <5m to plain TCP 8443 to avoid TLS handshake probe issues. That will mask TLS handshake failures but might keep unhealthy nodes in rotation; acceptable as an immediate mitigation to restore traffic while we debug origin TLS.

luca (prod-eng): Before changing checks, we need to confirm not routing bad traffic to unhealthy nodes. Can we temporarily set the NLB target group deregistration delay to 10s and lower the healthy threshold to 1? That will speed replacement and reduce error window.

jamie (networking): Yes we can. Plan: (A) set TG deregistration delay -> 10s and healthy threshold -> 1 (B) switch NLB healthcheck to TCP 8443 (C) monitor 2m and revert if error rate increases.

sasha (oncall): Go ahead with (A) and (B). Jamie's you’re doing changes — paste commands and confirm after. Priya please keep customer updated: we’ll try a quick mitigation and then propose a controlled rollback of their SG rule if needed.

jamie (networking): running commands now:

```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:.../tg-sunnova --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=10 Key=healthy_threshold_count,Value=1
aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn arn:.../tg-sunnova --health-check-protocol TCP --health-check-port 8443
```

jamie (networking): changes applied. Verifying target health...

```
# after changes
Target 10.0.12.45: healthy
Target 10.0.12.46: healthy
Target 10.0.12.47: healthy
```

sasha (oncall): Monitoring metrics (p95 latency, error-rate, HTTP 5xx) — show graphs?

luca (prod-eng): quick snapshot from monitoring: error-rate on Sunnova front-door dropped from 18% -> 2.2% over the last 90s, p95 latency unchanged. ALB healthchecks still show occasional TLS error but traffic is flowing.

priya (acct-mgr): Chatting with Sunnova now — they say traffic looks better on their side, some requests still 503 but much reduced. They asked what caused it.

jamie (networking): initial theory: customer changed security group to tighten TLS ciphers -> ALB handshake failures with NLB TCP health probes (which are TLS-aware currently). Our ALB->backend TLS negotiation was failing intermittently, causing targets to be marked unhealthy. By switching to TCP checks we avoided the handshake in healthchecks and allowed healthy nodes to serve.

tom (infra): Can we schedule an immediate joint troubleshooting window with their infra team to get the exact SG delta + TLS config? We should avoid long-term use of TCP healthchecks for TLS-terminated backends. Also need to validate we didn’t reintroduce capacity issues (we reduced dereg delay).

sasha (oncall): Good point. Priya please ask Sunnova for the SG diff (before/after) and if they rotated certs or changed ALPN/cipher suite. Also ask whether they had a canary for the change.

priya (acct-mgr): On it. Sunnova says they rolled a policy change via their infra automation: blocked outbound 443 from helper subnet; they thought it only affected egress to third-party telemetry. They didn’t realize it impacted ALB backend TLS handshake probes from the NLB. They’re patching now and can rollback rule in 15m if needed.

sasha (oncall): Plan B (if they can rollback): Request rollback, then switch healthchecks back to HTTP/TLS path and revert dereg delay. If they can't rollback, we’ll schedule a short maintenance to coordinate cipher compatibility.

jamie (networking): For rollback procedure (for Sunnova infra): remove deny rule for outbound 443 in helper subnet OR allow traffic to ALB backend CIDR x.x.x.0/24. After rollback, re-run healthchecks and confirm.

priya (acct-mgr): Sunnova agrees to rollback now and will confirm when done. ETA 12m. I’ll watch.

[some time passes]

priya (acct-mgr): Sunnova confirms rollback applied. They changed the SG rule back and re-applied automation.

jamie (networking): switching NLB healthchecks back to TLS/HTTP now and restoring dereg delay/thresholds.

```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn arn:.../tg-sunnova --health-check-protocol HTTPS --health-check-port 8443 --health-check-path /health
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:.../tg-sunnova --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=300 Key=healthy_threshold_count,Value=3
```

jamie (networking): back to original settings. Targets stable and healthy. Monitoring shows errors down to 0.4% and p95 stable.

luca (prod-eng): marking customer impact as mitigated. Need follow-up: 1) runbook update to include recommended NLB healthcheck types for TLS-terminated ALBs 2) audit automation that changes outbound SGs in customer infra onboarding 3) postmortem with Sunnova and internal ops.

priya (acct-mgr): Sunnova wants a short post-incident call. I’ve proposed 30m slot later today. They appreciate the quick mitigation.

sasha (oncall): Handoff: I’ll raise a postmortem ticket, assign to Luca for runbook and Jamie for network recommendations, and Tom for infra guardrails. Incident status: RESOLVED (customer-facing traffic restored).

incident-bot: Incident closed at 1765004543. Severity downgraded to SEV3 for follow-up work.

sasha (oncall): Good work team. Add any notes to the ticket and include the exact commands/outputs for the postmortem.

jamie (networking): Will attach command logs and CloudWatch graphs.

priya (acct-mgr): I’ll set up the call and include the rollback timeline and screenshots from Sunnova.

luca (prod-eng): Follow-up action items: ["Update NLB/ALB healthcheck guidance in Private deployment runbook", "Add automated test to detect outbound SG denials affecting ALB handshakes", "Customer postmortem with Sunnova", "Consider a guardrail in onboarding to warn about outbound 443 denies"]

sasha (oncall): Closing thread. If any regression reappears reopen or page oncall.
